title.narrative: WWF Mekong in BALANCE; Building ambition for nature conservation 2024-2027

description.narrative: Att bidra till implementeringen av det globala ramverket för biologisk mångfald i Mekong-regionen, och till att hindra förlusten av biologisk mångfald och öka motståndskraften mot klimatförändringar.
To contribute to the inclusive delivery of the Global Biodiversity Framework in the Mekong region, and to halting and reversing biodiversity loss and increasing resilience to climate change.

The overall goal of the programme is to contribute to the inclusive and equitable delivery of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KM-GBF) under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in the Mekong Region and to halting and reversing biodiversity loss and increasing resilience to climate change. The programme has the following objectives:
- By 2027, responsible actors in four focal ministries for the convention of biodiversity have enhanced ambition, skills and partnerships to ensure revised National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) deliver inclusive and measurable nationwide conservation benefits/targets. Mekong in BALANCE will contribute through providing technical support to NBSAPs revisions to align them with the KM-GBF and provide platforms for non-state actors to ensure inclusive consultation processes.
- By 2027, advanced progress on KM-GBF target 3 on land and inland waters and recognition of indigenous and local communities rights through equitable and inclusive processes is made. Mekong in BALANCE will contribute by strengthening Other Effective area-based Conservation Measures (OECM) institutional and management capacity to identify, assess and register OECMs, and actively involving and building capacity of local communities, indigenous peoples and faith-based groups in the process.
- By 2027, a comprehensive and rights based framework is established integrating biodiversity and climate priorities into transnational river governance in the Mekong River, supporting resilience of the river system, its ecosystems and the people who depend on it. Mekong in BALANCE will contribute by co-creating an inclusive conservation plan with the aim of enhancing collaboration between member countries to deliver against the GBF inland water targets, conducting basin-wide conservation assessments, and identifying innovative OECM opportunities.
Update Major amendment of contribution Nov 2025
Mekong in Balance MiB is on its second year of implementation and was designed to run until end of 2027. Since the strategy for development cooperation for regional Asia is going to be phased-out, the program will only receive funding from Sida for activities up until 30th June 2026. Since the activity period will be shortened the objectives of the intervention has had to be revised.
MiB outcomes rely to a large extent on medium- to long-term processes (NBSAP implementation, OECM recognition, Systematic Conservation Plan (SCP) adoption). Sub-grants with WWF implementing partners SHOAL and Asean Centre for Biodiversity (ACB) were just beginning to scale in 2025. The phase-out will limit sub-grantee partners ability to deliver results since early termination of sub-grantee and consultant contracts will be a consequence. The regional SCP consultant contract (planned until end-2026) will need to be closed by mid-2026.
Updates on planned outcomes
Outcome 1 (NBSAPs): WWF had originally committed to at least three countries employing WWF inputs before submission, 50 non-state actor organisations engaged, and ministries integrating human rights principles. Outcome 2 (OECMs): The results framework anticipated large-scale area coverage and 25 OECMs identified as potential and candidate progressing to piloting registration by 2027. Currently countries are still in the capacity development stage, working with ministries to develop national guidelines and identification of potential sites.
The phase-out will mean only partial delivery is feasible on outcome 1 and 2.
Outcome 3 (Freshwater/SCP): The Lower Mekong systematic conservation plan (SCP) is just getting underway in 2025. This is multi-year process that will need continuity of technical and financial support and requires Mekong River Comission (MRC) and line agency buy-in. By 2027 WWF had planned for policy uptake within the MRC, a basin-wide SCP, and pilot projects. The endorsement/adoption of SCP requires deeper national-level line agency engagement and MRC processes, which extend beyond the exit timeline. Private sector engagement was planned to start in Year 3 (202627), leading to pilots and innovative financing models. Instead, the project will now prioritise developing an actionable conservation plan that complements the SCP. This shift ensures countries receive clear, practical guidance to operationalise SCP findingsdirectly supporting Outcome 3 and the uptake of priority conservation actions. This new activity enhances the projects impact by ensuring that the SCP is not an end-product but a foundation for actionable, country-led implementation beyond the projects lifespan.
WWF has provided Sida with a detailed workplan for the country offices and their focus and justification for resources during the phase-out.
WWF Cambodia Funds will support three key activities:
Finalisation of Updated NBSAP Targets & Follow-up Workshop Supporting MoE and national stakeholders to finalise Cambodias updated NBSAP targets and share key findings from the national NBSAP assessment workshop to strengthen alignment with the KMGBF. Completion of National OECM Guideline Development Working with government partners to finalise Cambodias OECM guidelines, including technical reviews and consultations to support national recognition and reporting pathways. 7th National Report Support & OECM Communication Assets Co-organising inputs for Cambodias 7th National Report to the CBD and producing targeted communication assets to document Cambodias OECM journey and increase understanding among government agencies, CSOs, and local communities. These activities will help ensure Cambodias NBSAP is fully aligned with the KMGBF, strengthen national capacity and frameworks for OECM identification and reporting, and improve visibility and understanding of OECMs to support progress toward KMGBF Target 3.
WWF Laos Funds will support five key activities:
Cascading the NBSAP to the Local Level (Nampoui NPA) Supporting the development of one Local Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (LBSAP) in Nampoui NPA to translate national priorities into site-level action. NBSAP Awareness & Dissemination Event Organising a national NBSAP Forum to raise awareness among government agencies, CSOs, and local stakeholders on the updated NBSAP and its implementation pathway. Sub-national and National OECM Consultations Convening consultation workshops to strengthen understanding of OECM criteria, support site identification, and build alignment across government levels. Piloting OECMs (35 Sites) Providing technical support to assess and pilot 35 potential OECM sites to advance national reporting and progress toward KMGBF Target 3. Facilitating a knowledge-exchange visit for Lao officials to learn from Thailands practical experience in identifying, assessing, and recognising OECMs. These activities will help operationalise Laoss NBSAP, strengthen institutional capacity for OECM identification and reporting, and foster cross-border learning with Thailand. Together, they directly contribute to advancing inclusive and measurable progress toward KMGBF Target 3.
WWF Myanmar
During the phase-out period, WWF-Myanmar will focus on sustaining progress on local biodiversity planning and advancing community-led conservation opportunities. Funds will support three key activities:
Action Plan & Fundraising Meeting for LBSAP Targets- Convening local partners and stakeholders to review LBSAP priorities, develop a practical action plan, and identify potential fundraising pathways to ensure continuity beyond the project period. OECM and ICCA Opportunities Workshop (Chiang Mai)-Supporting Myanmar partners to join a regional workshop on the OECM journey, exploring opportunities for community-led conservation (ICCA) and strengthening understanding of governance and recognition pathways. Development of OECM Communication Assets- Producing tailored communication materials to document Myanmars OECM journey and raise visability among CSO, and community partners. These activities will help secure continuity of local biodiversity planning, strengthen Myanmar stakeholders capacity on OECM and ICCA processes, and support the KMGBF Target 3 agenda.
WWF-Thailand During the phase-out period, WWF-Thailand will focus on sustaining momentum on NBSAP implementation, OECM development, and local biodiversity planning. Funds will support three key activities:
Two LBSAP workshops in the Lower Songkram River Basin. One targeted to the Association of Songkram River Protection and the second one for the Provincial Ramsar Committee to strengthen local biodiversity planning. A National Dialogue on NBSAPLBSAP implementation to align national targets with local action. A National Dialogue on OECMs to advance recognition and management mechanisms using national case studies. These activities reinforce Thailands ability to implement the KMGBF by improving coherence between national and local biodiversity plans and sustaining progress on OECM development beyond the project period.
WWF Vietnam Funds will support four key activities:
Development of the Provincial Biodiversity Action Plan (PBAP) for Da Nang Supporting Da Nang city to translate national commitments under the GBF and NBSAP into a practical, province-level biodiversity action plan, strengthening local implementation and coordination. National GBF & NBSAP Engagement Events Assisting the CBD focal ministry to organise national multi-stakeholder events that bring together government agencies, non-state actors, CSOs, youth groups, and local communities to strengthen understanding and participation in GBF and NBSAP implementation. Development of OECM Guidelines Preparing national guidelines that include OECM assessment criteria, recognition processes, and an implementation roadmap to support Vietnams progress on identifying and reporting OECMs. Awareness-Raising Campaign on OECMs Designing and delivering a communication campaign to improve understanding of OECMs among government partners, CSOs, local communities, and the public, and to support national momentum toward KMGBF Target 3. These activities will enable Vietnam to advance GBF implementation at both national and provincial levels, strengthen the enabling environment for OECM identification and reporting, and build broad awareness among stakeholders. Together, they support Vietnams progress toward KMGBF Target 3 and ensure sustained engagement beyond the projects final phase.

he program started with an inception phase from January to June 2024, and then implementation started in July 2024. Thus, the first report, on which the results below are gathered, only covered the period July- December 2024.
Outcome 1 (National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans NBSAP): • Cambodia submitted revised national biodiversity targets to the CBD Secretariat, integrating OECMs under Target 3. • Thailands NBSAP (20232027) was approved and presented at COP16, with WWF contributing technical inputs. • In Laos and Viet Nam, stakeholder consultations and technical assessments were conducted to align national targets with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KM-GBF). • In Myanmar, the project adapted to the political context by supporting community-led Local Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (LBSAPs).
Outcome 2 (Other Effective area-based Conservation Measures, OECMs): • Awareness-raising and introductory sessions were conducted in all four countries (Cambodia, Myanmar, Viet Nam, and Thailand). • Cambodia included OECM under target 3 in their draft NBSAP. Thailand selected three OECM demonstration sites across terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. Myanmar identified 56 potential OECM sites covering approximately 0.5 million hectares. Vietnam identified 10 potential OECM sites internally.
Outcome 3 (Systematic Conservation Planning, SCP): • Internal training and expert identification for SCP were completed. • Engagements were initiated with the Mekong River Commission (MRC) and national Mekong Committees. • The regional SCP workshop was postponed to January 2025 due to scheduling overlap with the MRC Council Meeting, with expert working groups to be formed thereafter.
